questions.question: Name the five requirements for sustaining life and give one reason each is needed.
questions.expected_answer: Energy: all life processes need energy, which comes from the Sun captured by plants in photosynthesis and passed to animals through food. Gases: oxygen is needed for respiration; carbon dioxide is needed by plants for photosynthesis; nitrogen is made usable by bacteria for proteins. Water: reactions in cells happen in water, it transports substances, is a raw material for photosynthesis and helps control temperature. Soil: anchors plants and supplies water and mineral nutrients, and houses decomposers. Favourable temperature: life's chemical reactions work only within a range, about 0 to 45 degrees Celsius for most organisms; too cold and cells freeze, too hot and proteins are damaged.

questions.question: Explain how a leopard depends on the Sun for energy, and why fish in a polluted dam may die on a hot night.
questions.expected_answer: Plants capture the Sun's energy by photosynthesis and store it in food; herbivores such as impala eat the plants; the leopard eats the herbivores, so its energy came originally from sunlight. In a dam polluted with fertiliser or sewage, algae grow excessively; warm water holds less oxygen; at night algae respire and when they die bacteria decompose them, using up dissolved oxygen, so fish cannot get enough oxygen through their gills and suffocate.

questions.question: Compare the Tsitsikamma forest and the Richtersveld using the five requirements, and explain the term limiting factor.
questions.expected_answer: Both receive sunlight and air. The Tsitsikamma has rain in every month, deep soil and mild temperatures, so all requirements are plentiful and life is abundant. The Richtersveld has very little rain, thin stony soil and very hot summers, so life is sparse and adapted, for example succulents storing water. A limiting factor is the requirement in shortest supply that limits how much life an area can support; in the Richtersveld it is water.
